431: ## NEW_PID_EXT
432: 
433: | 1    | N      | 4    | 4        | 4          |
434: | ---- | ------ | ---- | -------- | ---------- |
435: | `88` | `Node` | `ID` | `Serial` | `Creation` |
436: 
437: Encodes an Erlang process identifier object.
438: 
439: - **`Node`** - The name of the originating node,
440:   [encoded as an atom](erl_ext_dist.md#utf8_atoms).
441: 
442: - **`ID`** - A 32-bit big endian unsigned integer.
443: 
444: - **`Serial`** - A 32-bit big endian unsigned integer.
445: 
446: - **`Creation`** - A 32-bit big endian unsigned integer. All identifiers
447:   originating from the same node incarnation must have identical `Creation`
448:   values. This makes it possible to separate identifiers from old (crashed)
449:   nodes from a new one. The value zero is reserved and must be avoided for
450:   normal operations.
451: 
452: `NEW_PID_EXT` was introduced in OTP 19, but only to be decoded and echoed back.
453: Not encoded for local processes.
454: 
455: In OTP 23 distribution flag
456: [`DFLAG_BIG_CREATION`](erl_dist_protocol.md#DFLAG_BIG_CREATION) became
457: mandatory. All pids are now encoded using `NEW_PID_EXT`, even external pids
458: received as [`PID_EXT`](erl_ext_dist.md#pid_ext) from older nodes.
459: 
460: In OTP 26 distribution flag [`DFLAG_V4_NC`](erl_dist_protocol.md#DFLAG_V4_NC)
461: became mandatory accepting full 64-bit pids to be decoded and echoed back.

585: ## NEWER_REFERENCE_EXT
586: 
587: | 1    | 2     | N      | 4          | N'       |
588: | ---- | ----- | ------ | ---------- | -------- |
589: | `90` | `Len` | `Node` | `Creation` | `ID ...` |
590: 
591: Encodes a reference term generated with `erlang:make_ref/0`.
592: 
593: - **`Node`** - The name of the originating node,
594:   [encoded as an atom](erl_ext_dist.md#utf8_atoms).
595: 
596: - **`Len`** - A 16-bit big endian unsigned integer not larger than 5.
597: 
598: - **`ID`** - A sequence of `Len` big-endian unsigned integers (4 bytes each, so
599:   `N'` = 4 \* `Len`), but is to be regarded as uninterpreted data.
600: 
601: - **`Creation`** - Works just like in
602:   [`NEW_PID_EXT`](erl_ext_dist.md#new_pid_ext).
603: 
604: `NEWER_REFERENCE_EXT` was introduced in OTP 19, but only to be decoded and
605: echoed back. Not encoded for local references.
606: 
607: In OTP 23 distribution flag
608: [`DFLAG_BIG_CREATION`](erl_dist_protocol.md#DFLAG_BIG_CREATION) became
609: mandatory. All references are now encoded using `NEWER_REFERENCE_EXT`, even
610: external references received as
611: [`NEW_REFERENCE_EXT`](erl_ext_dist.md#new_reference_ext) from older nodes.
612: 
613: In OTP 26 distribution flag [`DFLAG_V4_NC`](erl_dist_protocol.md#DFLAG_V4_NC)
614: became mandatory. References now can contain up to 5 `ID` words.
